text: Hi, I'm Sen, an AI interviewer. This call is transcribed. Ready to begin?
Tell me about a project you led and your role in it.
I worked on the payments ledger at my company. I wrote a lot of the Go code and fixed bugs. We moved to a new design and it went okay.
How would you design a rate limiter for a public API that serves many customers? Walk me through your approach.
I would count the requests each user makes per minute and block them if they go over the limit. I would keep the counts in a database and reset them every minute.
How would this work across multiple servers?
With multiple servers they would all use the same database for the counts, so it stays consistent. It might be a bit slow but that should be fine.
What happens when your shared store is unavailable?
If the database is down, I guess we would just let the requests through for a while until it comes back. I have not thought much about it beyond that.
Thank you. The team will review this and follow up. Goodbye.
